---
title: "Tests and verification"
---

Move trust from prose to executable evidence. A focused test or data contract should fail for the known defect, pass after repair, and be understandable to a reviewer. Also inspect final tables, figures, manifests, warnings, and uncertainty; green code is not a valid interpretation by itself.

Useful checks include uniqueness and referential integrity, allowed values and missingness rules, expected row counts, reproducible seeds, file hashes, and a small smoke run. Ask the agent to show the command and output, then run it yourself when the result matters.

Optional project instructions can encourage an epistemic distinction between observation and inference, but this workshop does not impose a mandatory final-status vocabulary. Evaluate whether such instructions improve behaviour or merely add boilerplate.
